supported_interpretation: The original baseline uses byte-identical logical and native ISA OpenQASM in all three bases in scan-05 and refine-01; no circuit rewrite explains its lower score.

Record/PUB/QPY metadata, shot counts, and independent raw-count estimates agree. The three original-baseline correlations all deteriorate, and two other orientations on data pair 1-2 also perform poorly in refine-01.
The recorded q1 calibration values and dates do not change. These are compilation-time snapshots, not contemporaneous evidence that the device remained unchanged during execution.

The result supports a temporal or workload-dependent change in measured device performance, consistent with hardware drift; it does not identify a unique causal error channel or prove q1 itself was the cause.
The workloads differ in candidate mix, randomized ordering, shots per circuit, execution time, and Batch versus job context. Exact circuit identity alone does not control these job-level conditions.

The approximately 7.84-percentage-point reset-minus-original gap combines a different physical layout with a degraded reference; the same-layout reset increment is approximately 0.513 percentage points and remains exploratory.
Reset and delay variants remain distinct native circuits: both explicit resets survive; the two 200us delays act on separate physical data qubits with one delay-only DAG layer.
